arxiv-2012-11523.title: Low-lying electron energy levels in three-particle electron-muon ions ( μ ​ e ​ L ​ i ) (\mu eLi) , ( μ ​ e ​ B ​ e ) (\mu eBe) , ( μ ​ e ​ B ) (\mu eB)
arxiv-2012-11523.creator: A. E. Dorokhov, V. I. Korobov, A. P. Martynenko, F. A. Martynenko
arxiv-2012-11523.description: Abstract The electron Lamb shift ( 2 ​ P − 2 ​ S ) (2P-2S) and the energy interval ( 2 ​ S − 1 ​ S ) (2S-1S) in muon-electron ions of lithium, beryllium, and boron have been calculated within the framework of the perturbation theory method for the fine structure constant and the electron-muon mass ratio.

arxiv-2107-13841.title: Addressing materials’ microstructure diversity using transfer learning
arxiv-2107-13841.creator: Aurèle Goetz, Ali Riza Durmaz, Martin Müller, Akhil Thomas, Dominik Britz, Pierre Kerfriden, Chris Eberl
arxiv-2107-13841.description: Abstract Materials’ microstructures are signatures of their alloying composition and processing history. Therefore, microstructures exist in a wide variety. As materials become increasingly complex to comply with engineering demands, advanced computer vision approaches such as deep learning (DL) inevitably gain relevance for quantifying microstrucutures’ constituents from micrographs.

arxiv-2307-11337.title: Fundamental CRB-Rate Tradeoff in Multi-Antenna ISAC Systems with Information Multicasting and Multi-Target Sensing
arxiv-2307-11337.creator: Zixiang Ren, Yunfei Peng, Xianxin Song, Yuan Fang, Ling Qiu, Liang Liu, Derrick Wing Kwan Ng, Jie Xu
arxiv-2307-11337.description: Abstract This paper investigates the performance tradeoff for a multi-antenna integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system with simultaneous information multicasting and multi-target sensing, in which a multi-antenna base station (BS) sends the common information messages to a set of single-antenna communication users (CUs) and estimates the parameters of multiple sensing targets based on the echo signals concurrently.

arxiv-2312-08513.title: Inelastic scattering of transversely structured free electrons from nanophotonic targets: Theory and computation
arxiv-2312-08513.creator: Austin G. Nixon, Matthieu Chalifour, Marc R. Bourgeois, Michael Sanchez, David J. Masiello
arxiv-2312-08513.description: Abstract Recent advancements in abilities to create and manipulate the electron’s transverse wave function within the transmission electron microscope (TEM) and scanning TEM (STEM) have enabled vectorially-resolved electron energy loss (EEL) and gain (EEG) measurements of nanoscale and quantum material responses using pre- and post-selected free electron states.

arxiv-2410-16296.title: Large Scale MRI Collection and Segmentation of Cirrhotic Liver
arxiv-2410-16296.creator: Debesh Jha, Onkar Kishor Susladkar, Vandan Gorade, Elif Keles, Matthew Antalek, Deniz Seyithanoglu, Timurhan Cebeci, Halil Ertugrul Aktas, Gulbiz Dagoglu Kartal, Sabahattin Kaymakoglu, Sukru Mehmet Erturk, Yuri Velichko, Daniela Ladner, Amir A. Borhani, Alpay Medetalibeyoglu, Gorkem Durak, Ulas Bagc
arxiv-2410-16296.description: Abstract Liver cirrhosis represents the end stage of chronic liver disease, characterized by extensive fibrosis and nodular regeneration that significantly increases mortality risk. While magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) offers a non-invasive assessment, accurately segmenting cirrhotic livers presents substantial challenges due to morphological alterations and heterogeneous signal characteristics.

arxiv-2502-13123.title: No Evidence of Asymmetrically Enhanced Star Formation in Infalling Galaxies in UNIONS Facilities: CFHT
arxiv-2502-13123.creator: Lauren M. Foster, Laura C. Parker, Stephen Gwyn, Ian D. Roberts, James E. Taylor, Michael J. Hudson, Alan W. McConnachie, Thomas de Boer
arxiv-2502-13123.description: Abstract Ram pressure stripping is a well-known environmental quenching mechanism that removes gas from galaxies infalling into groups and clusters. In some extreme examples of ram pressure stripping, galaxies with extended gas tails show evidence of enhanced star formation prior to quenching.

arxiv-2504-10599.title: Dust continuum radiation maps from MHD simulations of accretion-ejection systems around single and binary stars
arxiv-2504-10599.creator: Somayeh Sheikhnezami Christian Fendt Sareh Ataiee
arxiv-2504-10599.description: Abstract We study the launching of magnetized jets from a resistive circumstellar disk within a binary system, employing a unique combination of 3D MHD jet launching simulations (PLUTO code) and post-processed 3D radiative transfer modeling (RADMC-3D code). Our findings reveal a well-defined jet originating from the inner region of the disk, extending to a larger disk area.

pmc-11479499.description: Cadmium (Cd) and lead (Pb) exposure have been identified as risk factors for Helicobacter pylori seropositivity, possibly due to the immune suppression by Cd and Pb. Physical activity (PA) can induce an immune response. However, whether PA can reduce the effect of Cd and Pb on H pylori infection remains elusive.

pmc-12110555.description: BackgroundHypertension is becoming a burden globally with a significant shift in developing countries resulting from rapid urbanization with associated changes in lifestyles. pmc-12672378.title: Differential synaptic depression mediates the therapeutic effect of deep brain stimulation
pmc-12672378.creator: Jicheng Li, Jingheng Zhou, Bo He, Amy B Papaneri, Nicholas P Kobzar, Alan C Yeh, Ying Zhang, Guohong Cui
pmc-12672378.description: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) effectively treats drug-resistant neurological and psychiatric disorders, yet its mechanisms remain unclear. Here we show that high-frequency DBS of the subthalamic nucleus (STN), a common target for Parkinson’s disease (PD), activates afferent axons while inhibiting STN neurons.

pmc-13272142.title: Interventions for managing clinically relevant sleep disturbances or insomnia in cancer patients and survivors: an up-to-date systematic review and meta-analysis of self-reported sleep disturbance
pmc-13272142.creator: Julia Chan, Danielle Wing Lam Ng, Daniel Yee Tak Fong, Mathew Ching Hei Chan, Yijia Shi, Wendy Wing Tak Lam
pmc-13272142.description: BackgroundSleep disturbances are common after-effects of cancer. While the effectiveness of interventions in managing sleep disturbances in cancer have been evaluated, the effectiveness of interventions on reducing clinically relevant sleep disturbances remains unknown. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to appraise the effectiveness of up-to-date interventions managing clinical sleep disturbances in cancer patients or survivors.

pmc-13547424.creator: Rohan Saini, Sarah Fidler, Marta Boffito, Vicky Tittle, Nicolo Girometti, Gary Whitlock, the Dean Street Collaborative Group
pmc-13547424.description: BackgroundIn settings with high uptake of HIV pre‐exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), an increasing proportion of individuals newly diagnosed with HIV report prior PrEP exposure.
